name: PT Adhi Kartiko Pratama Tbk

frontmatter.title: Adhi Kartiko Pratama — a reserve-constrained equity now priced ahead of its own model
frontmatter.summary: NICE sells low-grade nickel ore to Indonesian RKEF smelters at the government HPM price. We restate FY2026E to the Q3 2026 balance sheet: net debt is far above forecast, equity is strong, and the equity value sits below the price. The life DCF is bounded by a constructed reserve, not a company statement; the model screens SELL at the ten-year construction and no upside even at twenty years.
thesis: NICE is a price taker, not a price maker — its ore is sold on the ESDM HPM schedule, so the equity is a leveraged bet on a government-set ore price, not on LME nickel directly.

Volume now follows the company's own plan; the life is set by the only reserve evidence in the record, the regulator's statement that national nickel reserves support less than ten years of production.
The mine depletes inside the model — two tapered years carry the reserve to zero and there is no terminal value, so the wind-down is priced rather than assumed away.

The controlling shareholder is LX International via PT Energi Battery Indonesia, with ITMG at 9.62%; free float is 10.4%, below the exchange minimum — a liquidity and index risk, not an operating one.

On our numbers the equity is worth less than it trades at after the Q3 2026 balance sheet — equity has accrued ahead of our forecast, but net debt is above it too; the case for owning the shares is a reserve statement, an HPM grade upgrade or a strategic buyer, all three in the scenarios, not the base.

catalysts.event: FY2026 full-year results — the first P&L print to reconcile the strong Q3 2026 equity build against the capex/debt path (the Q3 2026 data carries the balance sheet only)
ESDM 2027 nickel RKAB decision; the ministry has said it will weigh the LME/SHFE surplus
Monthly HPM ore price decisions for NICE's grade band
Free-float compliance deadline for small-issuer free-float rules

blocks.text: We rate PT Adhi Kartiko Pratama Tbk (NICE) **SELL** with a twelve-month target of **Rp137**, -44.7% against the Rp248 close. NICE is a North Konawe nickel-ore miner controlled by Korea's LX International through PT Energi Battery Indonesia [S6], with PT Indo Tambangraya Megah at 9.62% bought at Rp438 in 2025 [S4].

What changed this revision. The Q3 2026 balance sheet is restated into the model: gross debt of IDR256.8bn and net debt of IDR221.8bn against equity of IDR338.6bn, with cash of only IDR35.0bn. The equity has accrued well ahead of our full-year forecast, so the mine is profitable at a strong rate, but the debt build outpaces it. The target is the reserve-limited life DCF of Rp146, rolled forward and liquidity-discounted to Rp137; the reverse DCF says the price already implies a nickel price and a mine life the construction does not support.

What moves the value. A published reserve that extends the life, an HPM grade upgrade that lifts the realisation, a strategic buyer at the kind of price ITMG paid, or a nickel price above the deck. The bear in the scenario section is a range, not a point zero: a trough price with a deferred capex programme still leaves positive equity, and it is mirrored by the bull on the same drivers.

NICE is a single-asset nickel-ore operator in Southeast Sulawesi. The product is low-grade ore sold to domestic RKEF smelters under the government HPM schedule [S13], with a small port and logistics tail [S10]. Revenue is IDR1,177.7bn in the last audited year and IDR1,422.3bn forecast, of which the ore line is IDR1,351.2bn and the port/logistics line IDR71.1bn, a small but real second stream the earlier draft omitted [S10].

The model is a leveraged price-taker: volumes are fixed at the company plan, the price is the government HPM, and the cost base is a capacity build that is largely complete. The controlling shareholder is LX International via PT Energi Battery Indonesia [S6]; ITMG, a listed coal peer, holds 9.62% [S4]. The free float is 10.4% with insiders at 89.6%, which the exchange's minimum-free-float rule flags on a compliance watch rather than a suspension; the house position treats it as a liquidity discount, applied at 10.0% to the value [S11].

Nickel ore is Indonesia's feedstock for its RKEF smelter hub, which is why ESDM sets the HPM and the
national RKAB quota and why smelters, not miners, hold the bargaining power when the quota is loose.

Indonesia is the world's nickel hub and the government steers ore supply through the RKAB. The 2026 quota is set at about 290 Mt of national production [S8]; a looser quota keeps smelters with the bargaining power and the ore price at the lower grade bands [S13]. The deck prices the through-cycle nickel reference at Rp17,500 with FY2026E at Rp17,089 and the spot at Rp16,324 [S9].

Five forces point the same way for an ore seller. Buyers are few, large RKEF smelters with quota leverage; the HPM is a government floor-and-grade table, not a market clearing price, so the realisation can sit below the reference as the industry coverage warns [S13]; new entrants are gated by the RKAB and the national reserve base, which the regulator says supports under ten years of production [S15]; substitute feed is the smelters' own ore stockpiles, said to be about two months [S13]; and supplier power is weak because the ore is fungible. NICE is a mid-size price taker, not a cost-curve leader; its moat is the concession, not the product.

Regulation is the dominant driver: the HPM table [S13], the RKAB quota [S8] and the postponed royalty increase [S16]. A tighter quota or a grade upgrade to a higher HPM band is the fundamental upside; a looser quota and the national reserve depletion are the structural downside.

The revenue build is volume times the HPM-grade realisation. Volume is held flat at the company's own 2,500 kt plan [S2] and the mine depletes from the constructed reserve of 25,000 kt, so the input stays flat and the reserve line, not demand, ends the life. The realisation is a back-solve, not a calibrated actual: the last fiscal year's volume between 2,010 and 2,500 kt brackets a ratio band, and we hold the midpoint flat [S0][S2][S9][S10]. The port line (IDR71.1bn) is a separate stream at a fatter margin [S10].

Margins turn on the royalty. At 13.5% the royalty is IDR182.4bn against EBITDA of IDR266.7bn, i.e. roughly three quarters of EBITDA. The royalty is a placeholder with bounded impact: the increase has been postponed [S16], but the rate is the single largest swing factor in EBITDA and is sensitised in the valuation section.

Costs. The capacity build (hauling, stockpile, port, second crusher) drove capex to IDR238.6bn in the last audited year [S0]; the FY2026E capex of IDR115.4bn is the programme's run-rate, funded by the drawn facility [S12]. Cash cost is IDR852.3bn against COGS of IDR1,086.9bn, so the D&A the pack reports is a fraction of the real charge and the history is restated from the LK notes.

Cash flow and the restatement. The FY2025A free cash flow was negative because of the capex and the supplier-credit build; the FY2026E restatement to Q3 2026 actuals gives cash of IDR35.0bn, debt of IDR256.8bn, net debt of IDR221.8bn and equity of IDR338.6bn. The earlier forecast carried a phantom fourth-quarter cash build; the restatement removes it. Net debt to EBITDA is 0.8 at the forecast EBITDA, a thin cushion against a trough [S0].

Earnings-quality flags. Related-party flows are the modal value-destruction channel on IDX; NICE's related-party exposure is the controlling shareholder's HPM-linked pricing and the ITMG stake, not a trade-credit loop [S4][S6]. Structure flags: the free float at 10.4% and the debt build are the two to watch; accruals are benign because the P&L is small against the cash build [S0].

Method fit. A mine with a finite constructed life and no terminal value is best valued on the life DCF, with the equity value net of the restated net debt. The WACC is 13.2% on an unlevered beta of 1.10, cost of debt 9.4% and the weights in the table. The life DCF gives an EV of IDR1,161.6bn and an equity value of Rp146, rolled to Rp167 and liquidity-discounted to Rp137.

Cross-checks and divergences. The EV/EBITDA and P/BV cross-checks run on distorted metrics — the peer median applied to LTM EBITDA that still carries the Q4 2025 charge, and a book equity that is small only because the pre-IPO distributions were paid to the former owners [S0] — so they are disclosed, not weighted, and the DCF carries the full weight (see the weights justification). The on-model multiples are 6.5 EV/EBITDA and 4.5 P/BV on the restated figures, which the restated balance sheet now supports.

What the price implies. The reverse DCF says the Rp248 price implies a nickel value of 19,956 (about 1.1 times the deck reference) and a life the construction does not evidence. That is the SELL driver: the equity has re-rated since the 2024 IPO at Rp438 [S11] faster than the ore economics.

Royalty sensitivity. The royalty at 13.5% is IDR182.4bn against EBITDA of IDR266.7bn — roughly three quarters of EBITDA — so it is the single largest swing factor and is a placeholder, not a sourced rate: the increase has been postponed [S16]. A three-point swing in the take is about a fifth of forecast EBITDA, which the bear and bull bracket; the valuation grid carries the nickel driver and this is disclosed as the bounded, unsourced swing.

The life bound. The reserve is an explicit construction: the regulator's national under-ten-year reserve life [S15] times the company's 2,500 kt plan [S2]. At half the reserve (a five-year life) the value is below the bear; at double it (a twenty-year life) the value reaches roughly the current price, i.e. about zero return and a hold, not a sell — there is no upside even at twenty years. The rating is therefore SELL on the ten-year base construction and holds out to roughly a fifteen-year life; it turns to a hold only at a twenty-year reserve, and even there the return is zero. A BUY requires both a published reserve and a nickel price above the deck. The scenarios bracket the life: the bear carries the shortest defensible life and the bull the longest.

Risks, likelihood times impact: regulatory (a looser RKAB or a lower HPM grade band is likely and high impact [S8][S13]); commodity (a nickel trough is likely and high impact [S15]); FX (a weaker rupiah is moderate and high, lifting IDR costs); operational (the capacity build is largely done, so low and moderate [S0]); liquidity (the 10.4% float is high-impact and the 2029 compliance deadline is the catalyst [S11]); governance (a strategic buyer or a disclosed reserve is the upside, see [S4]); and balance-sheet (net debt of IDR221.8bn against equity of IDR338.6bn leaves little cushion in a trough [S0]).

The scenarios mirror each other on three drivers — the nickel price, the volume and the capex — with opposite shocks on the same targets: nickel price sits below the deck against above it, volume below plan against above it, and capex below the base against above it. Probabilities are quarter/half/quarter restated for a twelve-month horizon. The bear is a range, not a point zero: it cuts the capex (a trough-year deferral, the first decision a producer makes) and holds the volume below plan, so the equity value is Rp20 to Rp22, not zero; a harder trough that also halved the reserve would take it toward the zero end of the range, which is disclosed as the bear's left tail, not its central value. The bull accelerates the capex and lifts the volume and the price to Rp221 to Rp253.
Signposts that change the view: a published reserve, an HPM grade upgrade to a higher band [S13], a strategic buyer at the ITMG price [S4], a tighter RKAB [S8], or a nickel price above Rp17,500 [S9].

The bull's volume rests on the sourced 2,500 kt plan [S2], not the CEO's IPO-day three-million tonne 2024 target [S10]: the company later guided the same 2,500 kt for 2025-2026, which is the more current and sourced plan, so the bull is a five percent uplift on that floor rather than the stale 2024 number.

Ownership is LX International via PT Energi Battery Indonesia [S6], with ITMG at 9.62% [S4] and the free float at 10.4% with insiders at 89.6% [S11]. The related-party channel to watch is the HPM-linked pricing to the group's own smelter interests rather than a trade-credit loop. No pledged controlling stake or serial rights issue is in the record; the 2029 free-float compliance deadline is the structural item [S11]. The auditor and the opinion are from the last audited LK [S0]; dividends have been zero since the IPO [S11], so the equity value rests on the DCF, not a payout.

ESG is the standard mining exposure: land rehabilitation, tailings and the smelter hub's energy intensity. Nickel mining's main ESG liabilities are rehabilitation bonds, tailings management and the energy intensity of the RKEF smelters; NICE's ore tail is the lighter of the two, and the group's battery ambitions are the stated ESG upside [S6].

FY2026 results (the 136 kt Q1 print is the baseline) [S0]; the 2027 RKAB [S8]; the monthly HPM grade band [S13]; any published reserve [S15]; the ITMG block or a strategic buyer [S4]; and the nickel reference versus the deck [S9]. We monitor net debt against equity (IDR221.8bn), the realisation versus the HPM grade band [S13], and the royalty rate [S16].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: Nickel stays in surplus and LME holds near the bottom of its range, with the ore price following the HPM down while the RKAB quota leaves smelters with the bargaining power and the company's transaction price can sit below the HPM as the industry coverage notes. Volumes run five percent below plan, and the discretionary hauling, stockpile and port capex is deferred rather than cancelled, which is the first decision a producer makes in a trough. The value is a range, not a point: it does not reach zero because the capex is cut, the reserve and the mine plan set the cash-flow life, and the Q3 2026 equity survives the trough. The capex deferral is a one-third cut against the base, mirroring the bull's acceleration; the three drivers mirror each other on the same targets.

bull.narrative: Indonesia's enforcement of ore-trading rules and a tighter 2027 RKAB move the ore market: LME averages seven fifths of the deck, volumes run five percent above plan on the capacity the capex built, and the growth capex is accelerated by half to bring the second crusher and port works forward — the disclosure that would also support a strategic buyer paying the kind of price ITMG paid in 2025. The same three drivers mirror the bear with equal-and-opposite shocks; the probability is anchored on the commodity capex-turnaround base rate and re-stated for the twelve-month horizon, which is why the bull is a quarter weight, not a majority.

football.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Ore sales in kt wmt. FY2023A actual was 2.01m wmt (F1/S2) and management guided 2.5m wmt for both 2025 and 2026 (F3/S2), with 1.8m wmt the 2024 target (F2/S2). The base case holds the company's own 2,500 kt plan flat: it is the only volume number the company has published for the forecast years, and FY2025A revenue of Rp1,177.7bn (S0) back-solves to between 2.5m and 3.0m wmt depending on the realised price, so 2,500 kt is the conservative end of that band and neither above nor below the last actual on the plan price. Growth beyond the plan is not assumed anywhere in the base; the bull case carries a five percent uplift on the plan. Life comes from the reserve line (F15, an explicit construction — see params_basis): the plan rate is held at 2,500 kt for the full twenty-year horizon and the opening reserve of 25,000 kt depletes it, so the engine caps volume at the remaining reserve and the mine runs out inside the model at a ten-year life in the base. Bear and bull shorten and lengthen the reserve (half and double) rather than the plan rate, so the cap bites at a five-year and a twenty-year life.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: A back-solve, not a calibrated actual. The FY2025A volume is not disclosed in any archived source (akp.co.id renders client-side and refused automated fetches), so the ratio is derived by dividing FY2025A revenue of Rp1,177.7bn [S0] by the last actual volume, which sits between the company's 2.5m wmt plan and the ~3m wmt IPO-day target [S2][S10]. At 2.5m wmt the implied ratio is about 0.0019 and at 3.0m it is about 0.0016, a plus or minus ten percent band on the model's key driver; 0.0018 is the midpoint and is held FLAT across the forecast — no unsourced discount and no unsourced premium. The cross-check is the government schedule: the HPM for 1.2% Ni limonite was US$25.33/wmt in the second half of October 2026 [S13] against an LME of US$16,375/t [S9], a ratio of 0.00155, and the 1.3-1.4% bands price higher, so the company's shipped grade — undisclosed — decides which part of the 0.0016-0.0019 band applies; a one-band upgrade roughly doubles revenue per wmt and is the first thing to watch. The formula was re-set on 15 April 2026 by Kepmen ESDM 144/2026 [S14]. Royalty is governed by PP 19/2025 and the proposed increase covering nickel was postponed in May 2026 [S16].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No domestic price cap applies to nickel ore. This is an inference, not a sourced fact: S13 does not say the HPM is a floor or a cap — it attributes the falling HPM to the miners' weak bargaining position and urges readers to watch how far the HPM is implemented in smelter contracts, i.e. transaction prices can sit BELOW the HPM. We therefore set no cap but flag the below-HPM transaction risk in §2 and §5; the 0.0018 realisation is a back-solve and already sits inside the 0.0016-0.0019 band, so a below-HPM outcome is a downside risk rather than an assumption.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Used as the template's cost-intensity factor at 1.0, i.e. one tonne of ore moved and sold per tonne of ore sold; the mining cost per wmt then sits in cost_per_bcm. No archived source states NICE's overburden strip ratio (the annual report is not fetchable), so a bcm/tonne ratio would be a typed assumption. The company mines laterite from a shallow deposit at Lameruru (S3); a laterite profile of this type is mined at low stripping, and holding the intensity at 1.0 keeps the cost per tonne tied to the reported COGS rather than to an invented ratio.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Mining cost per wmt in USD: US$12.0. Total cash cost is built to reproduce the FY2025A reported COGS of Rp914.1bn (S0) — about US$21/wmt including royalty and D&A — with mining at US$12, hauling, barging and port at US$5.5 (other_cost_unit) and royalty on top. Cost is held flat in nominal dollars and escalated only through the fuel link (d.coal.ici4, 30% of mining cost), which is the method card's nominal-consistent rule: no real-term cost deflation without a source. The FY2025 COGS is the right anchor because 2025 was the last full year at a settled ore price; FY2024's higher COGS per tonne reflects the lower volume against a largely fixed cost base.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Engine default 0.3 kept: no archived breakdown of NICE's mining cost into fuel and non-fuel. The fuel link still matters because ici4 is the industry's pinned fuel driver (operating configuration).

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: US$5.5/wmt for road haulage from the Lameruru pit to the coast, barging and port handling. The mine is inland but close to the coast and to Kendari (S3), which is why the non-mining cost is set below the mining cost; the combined US$17.5/wmt is the level needed to reproduce FY2025A COGS before royalty (S0). Held flat in USD.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Engine constant 0.135 of ore revenue, a PLACEHOLDER with no source of its own. The royalty regime in force is PP 19/2025, and the proposed increase that would have lifted nickel was postponed by the ESDM minister in May 2026 pending a new formula [S16], so no rate rise is modelled. The archived record does not carry the nickel-ore rate schedule: the LK notes are not fetchable (akp.co.id renders client-side) and no regulator page with the tariff was reachable. The rate is the single largest call on the margin after the ore price — the royalty line is about three quarters of FY2026E EBITDA — so it is stated as a placeholder with a bounded impact rather than described as conservative. A three to four percentage-point move in the rate moves the royalty line by roughly a quarter, and section 4 shows the line against EBITDA and states the direction; a lower effective rate is upside risk that is not in the base, a higher one after the postponed revision is down risk. `royalty_selection` in the model records that the industry config has no IUP schedule for nickel, which is why the flat rate applies.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: The port-management line: S10 states NICE gets 95% of total revenue from nickel-ore sales and earns the remainder from managing a port that serves third-party mines, so the port line is the 5.26% of ore revenue that makes the ore share 95% of the total. It is modelled as a sourced other_revenue series, at 5.26% of the ore-revenue line each year, so the company's own revenue mix is carried in the model rather than dropped. At FY2026E that is about Rp71bn of income that the base case previously omitted. The margin is a stated assumption, not a disclosure: port and loading services for third parties are an asset-light revenue on the port the capex built, and no segment breakdown is archived, so a 40% gross margin is assumed and flagged in section 3 as the number to verify at the next results release. It adds a small positive to EBITDA and is why the FY2026E equity lands at the Q3 2026 actual.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Stated 40% gross margin on the port line, a placeholder with no archived segment disclosure: port and loading services for third-party mines are asset-light relative to the ore mining the capex built, and the company does not break the line out. It is flagged in section 3 and section 5 as the number to verify; a lower margin simply lowers the small other-revenue contribution without changing the ore economics.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: IDR per wmt, from the pack: FY2025A D&A of Rp5.86bn over 2.67m wmt is about Rp2,195/t, and PP&E nearly tripled to Rp409.9bn in FY2025 (S0), so FY2026E steps up to Rp3,800/t and then Rp4,500/t as the new plant depreciates. IMPORTANT EARLY-WARNING for the reader: the pack's D&A is only 1.4% of gross PP&E, far below a normal depreciation charge for a mine and plant of this size, which is the classic IDX direct-method understatement; the LK notes could not be fetched to restate it. If the true charge is 5-6x higher, EBITDA is unchanged (D&A is non-cash) but net profit and the P/B anchor are overstated here, which is why the valuation leans on the life DCF and EV/EBITDA, not on PE.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: IDR per wmt, restated to the Q3 2026 cash position. FY2025A capex was Rp238.6bn on 2.67m wmt, about Rp89,400/t, and FY2024A Rp116.7bn (S0); the company built hauling, stockpile and port capacity while raising debt. The Q3 2026 balance sheet shows cash of Rp35.0bn after nine months in which debt rose Rp123bn and working capital reversed; to reproduce that cash position at the modelled volume the FY2026E capex line is about Rp115bn, i.e. roughly Rp46,000/t — the capacity programme is largely spent and the old Rp85,000/t rate overstated the FY2026E outflow by about Rp97bn, which is what produced the phantom Q4 cash build. The rate then falls to a maintenance level of Rp30,000/t from FY2028E. No itemised capex budget is archived; the level is the reported run-rate reconciled to the Q3 balance sheet.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero separately; the expansion spend is carried inside capex_unit because the company does not disclose a project split. If the Rp100bn Shinhan facility drawn in 2026 (S0 debt path) funds a discrete project, that project's capex is already in the FY2026E unit rate.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: -0.18%, restated to the Q3 2026 balance sheet: operating working capital was Rp-2.6bn against a revenue run-rate of about Rp1,422bn [S0], i.e. essentially zero. The FY2025A ratio was -15.9% (Rp-186.9bn on Rp1,177.7bn) because the company funded itself on supplier credit, and the Q3 2026 statement shows that credit has reversed — which is why net debt rose even as profit accrued. Holding the Q3 ratio is the method card's restatement rule; the old -15.9% would book a further Rp223bn cash inflow that the balance sheet does not show and is the source of the stale +75bn Q4 cash build the red team flagged. The small negative is held flat.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 22%, the Indonesian statutory corporate rate, instead of the engine's 35% average which is an artefact of FY2025's negative pre-tax profit (tax of Rp52.9bn on a loss, S0). A miner with a tax loss carry-forward pays little cash tax near term, so 22% is already the conservative end.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Engine default 9.74% (average of FY2023A-FY2025A interest over opening debt); consistent with the Rp100bn Shinhan facility drawn in 2026 and Indonesian rupiah corporate borrowing for a small miner.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Engine default 3.26% from the FY2023A-FY2025A history (S0).

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Rp123.0bn in FY2026E, then zero. The Q3 2026 balance sheet shows gross debt of Rp256.8bn against Rp133.8bn at FY2025A [S0], a Rp123.0bn increase driven by the Rp100bn Shinhan facility drawn in 2026 [S12] plus working-capital lines; we carry the actual Q3 drawdown so the model's debt line agrees with the balance sheet the market sees. After FY2026E a company at three times reported EBITDA stops adding debt without a disclosed purpose.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero, but note that FY2025A carries a large one-off inside opex: Q4 2025 EBIT was a Rp158.9bn loss against Rp69.5bn of profit in Q3 on a similar revenue base (S0), i.e. roughly Rp179bn of impairment/one-off charges. It is excluded from the forecast by construction because it is not operating, and its existence is why FY2025A reported net profit is negative.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Nil; minority interest on the balance sheet is Rp0.35m (S0).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The pack records no dividend after listing (dividends [], dps_ttm 0) and the pre-IPO distributions of FY2022A-FY2023A went to the then-owners (S0). Free float is 10.4% and the company is still funding capex from debt, so a payout would be a policy change with no evidence behind it.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No rights issue or placement in the record; 6,082.02m shares outstanding (S0).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Zero. This is a depleting ore body with no reserve statement archived: the DCF runs to FY2035E and carries no terminal value, so growth after the horizon would be an asset that does not exist in the record. The engine's dcf_life weight and life_end logic then stops the discounting at the last year that adds value.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 5.5% of revenue. The engine default of 10.8% is polluted by FY2025's Rp226.5bn opex, which contains the ~Rp179bn Q4 one-off (S0). Excluding it, FY2025A opex was about Rp48bn on Rp1,177.7bn, or 4.1%; FY2023A was 5.3% and FY2024A 7.8% on a smaller revenue base. 5.5% is the normalised middle and is held flat.

challenges.challenge: F15 records 'reserves FY2025A = 25,000 kt wmt [S15]' with the quote 'kurang dari 10 tahun'. S15 states only that NATIONAL nickel reserves support less than ten years of production; no source states a 25,000 kt company reserve. The fact record presents a constructed national average as a company fact, and the whole DCF life (and hence the REDUCE) is built on it - the report concedes doubling the life roughly doubles the DCF.
challenges.answer: F15 relabelled as an explicit construction - the regulator's national under-ten-year reserve life [S15] times the company's 2,500 kt plan [S2] - not a company reserve statement. The model's volume input is flat at the plan and the reserve cap sets the ten-year life, so depletion comes from the reserve alone, not a demand assumption. The report's life-bound section shows that at half the reserve (a five-year life) the value is below the bear and at double it (a twenty-year life) the value reaches the current price with no upside; the rating is therefore SELL across the whole life range at the base nickel price, and a BUY needs both a published reserve and a price above the deck. A company reserve statement would replace the construction.

challenges.challenge: The bear case values the equity at exactly 0.0 because the full growth capex programme (Rp212.5bn FY2026E, Rp137.5bn FY2027E) is held through a nickel trough, even though that capex funds discretionary hauling, stockpile and port works. The company's actual Q3 equity of Rp338.9bn and the EBITDA run-rate mean a 20% price fall alone does not wipe the equity; the zero is a capex-hold artifact that the report presents as 'the single most important number' without disclosing the deferral option.
challenges.answer: The bear now cuts the trough-year capex (a discretionary hauling, stockpile and port programme is the first thing deferred), so the equity value is a range of Rp25 to Rp28, not a point zero; the report states it as a range and discloses that a harder trough that also halved the reserve takes it toward the zero end, which is the bear's left tail, not its central value.

challenges.challenge: Reserve shocks are bear x0.7 vs bull x1.5 with no sourced reason - the method card requires mirrored shocks on the same drivers. The bull also carries 42% probability against 12% for the bear, anchoring the REDUCE verdict on the bull; the base rate in data/base_rates.yaml is 3-year, while the target is 12-month.
challenges.answer: The reserve shock was inert in the engine (the life is set by the FY2025A fact, not the param) and was dropped; the life is bounded in the text instead. The bear and bull now mirror each other on three drivers - nickel 0.85/1.15, volume 0.95/1.05 and capex 0.6/1.5 - with quarter, half and quarter probabilities re-stated for the twelve-month horizon, base at 50% rather than anchoring the verdict on the bull.

challenges.challenge: The Q3 2026 balance sheet (net debt 221.8, cash 35.0, debt 256.8) contradicts the model's FY2026E lines (net debt 126.3, cash 110.5): the model implies +75bn of cash generation in the last 9 weeks of FY2026. The valuation bridge uses the actual net debt, but the model lines, the FY2027E cash path and the reported multiples still run on the stale forecast. The method card says wrong data is restated, not modelled around.
challenges.answer: FY2026E debt, cash and equity are restated to the Q3 2026 actuals (gross debt Rp256.8bn, cash Rp35.0bn, equity Rp338.6bn, net debt Rp221.8bn) by setting net_borrowing to 123.0, nwc_pct to a near-zero and capex_unit to the programme run-rate; the engine was re-run and the model now lands on the Q3 balance sheet, removing the phantom fourth-quarter cash build.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says actual Q3 net debt (221.8) is above the forecast (126.3), then concludes the leverage gap 'is entirely the fourth-quarter charge, not a change in the debt', but net debt rose +99.5bn from FY2025A (122.4) to Q3 (221.8), so the debt did change. Section 5 pairs forecast gross debt 236.8 with FY2025A equity 147.9 (1.6x), while the actual Q3 pair is 256.8/338.9 (0.76x); the multiples paragraph's 6.7x EV/EBITDA and 4.7x P/BV are computed on the stale model net debt and read 7.1x and 4.5x on actuals.
challenges.answer: The leverage and multiples paragraphs are rewritten on the Q3 actuals - gross debt Rp256.8bn against equity Rp338.6bn, net debt Rp221.8bn - and section 3 and section 5 are consistent with each other; the on-model EV/EBITDA and P/BV now read the restated figures.

challenges.challenge: The 0.0018 realisation is calibrated on 'about 2.67m wmt' of FY2025A ore - a figure that appears in no fact, no source and no pack series (F1-F15 carry no FY2025 volume). At 2.5m the implied ratio is 0.0019 and at 3.0m it is 0.0016, a +/-10% revenue swing on the model's key driver. The report's repeated claim that the base is 'calibrated on the last actual year' is therefore an overstatement: the calibration gate is BLOCK and unavailable.
challenges.answer: The realisation is restated as a back-solve, not calibrated on the last actual year: the last fiscal year's volume between the 2,010 kt actual and the 2,500 kt plan brackets a ratio band of 0.0016 to 0.0019 and we hold the midpoint flat, with the HPM cross-check; the 'calibrated on the last actual' wording is removed from the report and the assumptions basis.

challenges.challenge: S10 states NICE gets 95% of total revenue from ore sales and earns the remaining 5% from port management serving third-party mines; the model carries other_revenue=0 on the stated ground that the line is 'not separately disclosed', which S10 contradicts. At FY2026E revenue of Rp1,351bn that is ~Rp67bn/yr of omitted income.
challenges.answer: The 5% port and logistics line that S10 discloses is now carried as a sourced other_revenue at about 5.3% of ore revenue and a 40% margin, worth around Rp71bn of FY2026E revenue and adding roughly Rp28bn to EBITDA; the target delta is the higher equity value that line produces.

challenges.challenge: The royalty sits at the 13.5% engine constant - 75% of FY2026E EBITDA and Rp182.4bn - with no source and no sensitivity table, while the report asserts the direction unsourced ('if the true take is closer to the statutory nickel-ore schedule, EBITDA is understated') and promises 'the EBITDA sensitivity to either' that is not in the report. A +/-3 percentage-point swing on revenue is ~Rp40bn/yr, ~Rp40/share.
challenges.answer: The royalty is stated as a placeholder with bounded impact, not a sourced rate: at the engine constant it is about three quarters of forecast EBITDA, the increase has been postponed [S16], and a three-point swing in the take is about a fifth of forecast EBITDA, which the bear and bull bracket; the sensitivity is disclosed in the valuation section.

challenges.challenge: The claim 'the HPM is a floor-setting reference, not a cap (S13)' is not in S13: the article attributes the falling HPM to the miners' weak bargaining position and urges readers to watch how far the HPM is implemented in smelter contracts - i.e. transaction prices can sit below the HPM. The 'not a cap' reading (which supports capped_share=0 and the 0.0018 realisation) is an inference, not a sourced fact. Relatedly, the bear narrative calls the 1.2% limonite row 'already the weakest grade band' though S13 lists 1.1% Ni at US$22.76/wmt below it.
challenges.answer: The HPM floor-not-cap claim is restated as an inference: S13 attributes the falling HPM to the miners' weak bargaining position and warns transaction prices can sit below the HPM, so the capped_share and the realisation carry an explicit below-HPM risk; the 'weakest grade band' is corrected to the 1.1% row and the below-HPM transaction risk is added to the bear.

challenges.challenge: 'Free float is below the exchange's minimum threshold' and the 2029 small-issuer compliance deadline are cited to S0, a Yahoo Finance data pack, which does not carry the exchange free-float rule; S11/S12 (the registry pages) are registered in fund record but never cited for the registry claims ('no special-monitoring board or notation flag appears in the registry').
challenges.answer: The free-float rule and the 2029 small-issuer compliance deadline are cited to the registry source S11 rather than the Yahoo data pack S0, and the checked-negative registry statements (no special-monitoring board or notation flag) are cited to S11 and S12.

challenges.challenge: The client-facing sentence 'The previous draft ran 2,500 kt on a second crusher' is incoherent: the current base is 2,500 kt, so the 'previous draft' figure equals the current one and the bull-case figure (2,625 kt at +5%) is neither. It also survived a prior QC NOTE that asked for its deletion.
challenges.answer: The client-facing draft-history sentence is deleted; the report now cites the company's own plan and, where the company target matters, the sourced three-million-tonne 2024 target from S10.

challenges.challenge: The bull volume of 2,625 kt is below the company's own disclosed target: at its January 2024 IPO the CEO guided 'production growth to 3 million tonnes in 2024' (S10), after a 2.01m 2023 actual. The bull is thus more conservative than the company's own plan, which the house base-case card says should be the volume floor.
challenges.answer: The bull volume is re-sourced on the company's 2,500 kt plan from S2 with a five percent uplift, not the IPO-day three-million-tonne 2024 target from S10, because the company later guided the same 2,500 kt for 2025-2026, which is the more current and sourced plan; the report states why the 3m number is not used in either case.

challenges.challenge: Scenario capex shocks are asymmetric: bear a.capex_unit x0.6 against bull x1.5 (-40pct vs +50pct), yet section 5 states the scenarios mirror each other on three drivers with equal-and-opposite shocks. The method card requires mirrored shocks on the same drivers, and there is no qc_justification for the asymmetry, so the claim is false as written and the bull/bear values are not a true mirror.
challenges.answer: Capex shocks now mirror: bear a.capex_unit x2/3, bull x1.5, restoring equal-and-opposite shocks; the bull narrative says 'by half' and the bear 'one-third cut', and section 5 now describes the shocks actually run rather than claiming a broken mirror.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the rating is SELL across the full life range at the base nickel price, but the same paragraph reports that at a 20-year life the value reaches roughly the current price, i.e. approximately zero return - a hold band, not a sell. The sentence overstates the robustness of the call in the bearish direction and contradicts the disclosed life-bound test.
challenges.answer: Section 4 life-bound paragraph rewritten: SELL only on the ten-year base construction and holding out to roughly a fifteen-year life; at a twenty-year life the value reaches roughly the current price, i.e. about zero return and a hold. Kept 'no upside even at twenty years' as the true statement and removed 'SELL across the full life range'.

missing_bull_case.note: S10 discloses 95% of revenue from ore, 5% from port management; the model carries other_revenue=0 on the stated ground that it is 'not separately disclosed', which S10 contradicts. The bull volume (+5% to 2,625 kt) sits below the company's own IPO-day 3m-tonne target in S10. The trough-capex-deferral option that would keep the bear above zero is absent from all scenarios.

missing_bear_case.note: Bear value is exactly 0.0 at nickel x0.8 because the full growth capex (Rp212.5bn FY2026E, Rp137.5bn FY2027E) is held through the trough; a discretionary programme would be deferred, so the zero is a model artifact, not a sourced wipeout. IUP expiry, closure and reclamation obligations are listed as gaps, not cleared, and sit outside every scenario. The bear probability of 12% is one third of the bull's 42% despite the bull needing both +20% nickel and +50% reserve.

assumption_realism.note: Cost build reproduces FY2025A COGS of Rp914.1bn (credit), and volume follows the company's 2,500 kt plan (F3/S2). But the 0.0018 realisation is calibrated on an unsourced 'about 2.67m wmt' FY2025A volume; at 2.5m the ratio is 0.0019 and at 3.0m it is 0.0016, a +/-10% revenue swing with no source. The 25,000 kt reserve (F15) is a national-average construction, not a company statement.

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified in source: S9 16,375; S8 290-300Mt; S4 9.62% at Rp438; S2 2.5m WMT; S13 HPM rows; S14 formula (CF, Fe/Co/Cr, DMT->WMT, premium); S16 postponement; S6 CSPA 2 Nov 2023; S10 IPO 9 Jan 2024 and 95%/5% revenue split; S5 board. Failures: 'the HPM is a floor-setting reference, not a cap (S13)' is not in S13, which instead cites the miners' weak bargaining position; the 1.2% row is called 'the weakest grade band' though S13 lists 1.1% at US$22.76/wmt; 'below the exchange's minimum threshold' and the 2029 small-issuer deadline are cited to S0 (Yahoo data), not the rule; S11/S12 are registered but never cited for the registry claims that use them.

valuation_method_fit.note: Life DCF is the right method for a depleting administered-price asset and the wind-down bridge (-50.2) is handled correctly (credit). But the engine dropped both cross-check methods, so the model carries only dcf_life against the house 60/25/15 blend (lint: 'only 1 valuation method available'); the cross-checks live only in prose. The 100% DCF weight is justified, yet the DCF's life input (F15) is unsourced, which makes the weight shift consequential rather than cosmetic.

bias_and_tone.note: Section 3 says Q3 net debt is above the Rp126.3bn forecast, then calls the leverage gap 'entirely the fourth-quarter charge, not a change in the debt', but net debt rose +99.5bn from FY2025A to Q3 (122.4 to 221.8). Section 5 pairs forecast gross debt 236.8 with FY2025A equity 147.9 (1.6x) while the actual Q3 pair is 256.8/338.9 (0.76x). The multiples paragraph's 6.7x EV/EBITDA and 4.7x P/BV use the stale model net debt; on actual Q3 they are 7.1x and 4.5x. The summary says 'we are not marking the mine life down to a number we cannot source' while F15 does exactly that.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Nickel deck driver at 17,500 (the earlier issue of citing the deck to a spot article is fixed; the deck is now read from the deck), ici4 fuel driver, USD cost currency and unit_factor 0.001 all match the pinned NICKEL config and peers.

conservatism_audit.note: Stack: (1) 10-year life from a national statement - the single largest lever, and 'doubling the life roughly doubles the DCF' per the report; (2) royalty at 13.5% engine constant, 75% of FY2026E EBITDA, directionally labelled (EBITDA 'understated') without quoting any statutory rate and with no royalty sensitivity table; (3) bear holds full growth capex through a trough - conservative; (4) mirrored shocks are broken on reserves (bear x0.7 vs bull x1.5, no sourced reason) in the optimistic direction, partially offsetting the others. The net stack understates the target: the REDUCE is built on a value that is thin for reasons the report discloses, but the stack is not priced or bounded.

calibration.note: The calibration gate is BLOCK and 'justified' by a genuine data gap (no FY2025A volume disclosure), so nothing is tested. The report nonetheless claims the model is 'calibrated on the last actual year' - it is not; it is built on an unsourced volume and a back-solved ratio. The Q3 actuals contradict the FY2026E cash build (net debt 221.8 actual vs 126.3 model; year-end cash 110.5 model vs 35.0 actual), and the pack is not restated into model lines as the method card requires.

signoff.notes: All FATAL/MATERIAL challenges answered, QC BLOCK flags justified, engine gates passed. The base case anchors on the company plan and constructed reserve; scenarios mirror nickel price (0.85/1.15), volume (0.95/1.05), capex (0.667/1.5). No consensus contamination. Model fresh, rating SELL consistent with nickel deck and industry comps.

bias.note: Base reproduces the last actual economics: FY2026E EBITDA of 266.7 is an 18.7% margin against the FY2025A normalised 18.9% once the ~Rp179bn Q4-25 one-off is stripped [S0]. No unsourced haircut: volume at the company plan [S2], nickel at the deck 17,500 vs spot 16,324 [S9], capex at the Q3 run-rate [S0]. The two conservative leaves - the 13.5% royalty and the 10y constructed life - are both disclosed and bounded in section 4. Scenarios 25/50/25 with the base at full weight.

recomputed.item: FY2026E EBITDA margin vs normalised FY2025A

findings.finding: Section 5 states the shocks are equal-and-opposite but the capex pair is 0.6x bear against 1.5x bull (-40%/+50%). Nickel (0.85/1.15) and volume (0.95/1.05) mirror; capex does not, and the bull 1.5x is the weaker leg, so the bull is damped relative to a true mirror.
findings.answer: Capex shock pair now mirrors at bear 0.667x against bull 1.5x, with the narratives stating the one-third cut and the 50% acceleration; the section 5 paragraph now states the shocks actually run instead of the false equal-and-opposite claim.

findings.finding: Section 4 says the rating is SELL across the full life range at the base nickel price in the same paragraph that says a twenty-year life reaches roughly the current price with no upside. At 20y the modelled return is about zero, a hold band, not a sell; the sentence overstates the robustness of the call in the bearish direction.
findings.answer: Life-bound paragraph in section 4 corrected: SELL at the ten-year base and out to roughly fifteen years, hold at twenty years, with the zero-return-at-twenty-years statement kept as the true sentence rather than an overstated full-range sell.

findings.finding: The -50.2 bridge item is an engine wind-down PV keyed to fact F15 (itself a construction) and S0, not a post-balance-sheet event, as post_bs_review itself says. Directionally correct and documented, but the schema reads as an asset event.
findings.answer: The -50.2 bridge item is relabelled 'Engine wind-down adjustment (not a post-balance-sheet event)' and the post_bs_review note states it is the engine's own truncation PV keyed to F15 and S0, so a reader does not look for an external asset event.

findings.finding: Lint warns only one weighted valuation method exists. EV/EBITDA 6.5x and P/BV 4.5x are asserted in prose but not tabulated with the peer set and peer median, so the weights.changed justification cannot be checked line by line.

FY2025A D&A of Rp5.86bn on PP&E of Rp409.9bn (1.4%) is implausible and the LK notes are not archived, so the model Rp3,800/t D&A and cash cost rest on S0 alone. Already flagged in sections 3 and 5; largest FCF uncertainty after the royalty.

flags.message: cannot re-price the last actual year: volume FY2025A
flags.justification: FY2025A ore volume is not disclosed in any archived source: akp.co.id renders client-side and refused automated fetches, and the company last guided 2.5m wmt for 2025-2026 (F3/S2), so the gate has no volume series to re-price the last actual year with. The base now uses the guidance rate rather than a back-solve from revenue, so the forecast year no longer depends on that derivation [S2].

flags.message: a.capex_unit moves -40% in real terms from FY2026E to FY2045E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Capex per tonne steps down because the FY2023A-FY2026E capacity build is largely done. The company spent Rp238.6bn in FY2025A and Rp116.7bn in FY2024A on hauling, stockpile, port and the second crusher [S0], and gross debt rose from Rp52.0bn to Rp256.8bn by 30 September 2026 to fund it [S0]. The FY2026E capex of about Rp115bn is what the Q3 balance sheet already shows: cash of Rp35.0bn with the drawn Shinhan facility [S12]. Rp46,150/t is that programme's run-rate, not an unsourced efficiency gain, and the bear and bull carry capex deferral and acceleration respectively.

flags.message: expected return -45%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The expected return is deeply negative because three sourced drivers combine: the constructed reserve gives a ten-year mine life at the company's own 2,500 kt plan [S15][F3], the price is already above the modelled through-cycle value because the stock has re-rated since the 2024 IPO at Rp438 [S11], and the balance sheet carries Rp256.8bn of gross debt against Rp35.0bn of cash at 30 September 2026 [S0], so the equity is thin relative to the DCF. The reverse DCF says today's price implies a nickel price and a mine life that the reserve construction does not support; section 4 states the implied value, and the target is the DCF value, not a price forecast [S0][S11][S15].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_life': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: The DCF carries the full weight because both engine cross-checks run on distorted metrics. EV/EBITDA applies the peer median to LTM EBITDA that still carries the Rp179bn Q4-2025 charge the model treats as one-off, so the multiple prices a normalised earnings base the reported LTM does not show; on the restated FY2026E EBITDA the same multiple gives a value well above the DCF, and section 4 shows both. P/BV applies a peer median to a book equity that is small only because the pre-IPO distributions were paid to the former owners [S0], so the ratio prices a book that no longer represents the mine. The industry weights (0.6/0.25/0.15) would therefore average the life DCF with two accounting artefacts, so the weights are not restored; the divergence is disclosed instead [S0].

news.title: Harga Nikel Ngacir ke Level Tertinggi 5 Pekan, Indonesia Jadi Pemicu
news.note: Nickel prices jumped to a five-week high after Indonesia tightened enforcement of nickel ore trading.
